questions.question: How big should the Jawa scavenging system be at its core?

options.label: Skill only
options.description: Buys: exactly your ruling, a better Jawa brings home more rare parts. Costs: about a day of work, but the player never makes a choice; it happens out of sight.

options.label: Strip, then sort at home (Recommended)
options.description: Why: smallest version with a real reveal. Buys: wrecks give metal plus unsorted crates; your best appraiser sorts them at the scrap shrine and finds the treasure. Costs: about two weeks, a bench and crate art, and more hauling.

options.label: Full scavenging process
options.description: Buys: survey a wreck first, choose how to cut it apart, then sort at home; the richest version. Costs: four weeks or more, lots of writing for wreck stories, and more steps per wreck that players must learn.

options.label: Sort only, no field changes
options.description: Buys: the reveal moment at home without touching how wrecks are stripped. Costs: about a week, but skill on site stops mattering, which is half of your ruling.

questions.question: Which skill should decide how well a Jawa strips a wreck on site?

options.label: Construction (Recommended)
options.description: Why: the game already trains Construction when taking things apart. Buys: no surprises for players, and Jawa already have a Construction gift. Costs: builders and scavengers are the same people.

options.label: Crafting
options.description: Buys: scavenging reads as fine handwork, and splits from building. Costs: goes against the game, which still trains Construction while stripping; feels odd.

options.label: Better of the two
options.description: Buys: any skilled Jawa is useful; forgiving. Costs: blurs who the clan's real scavenger is; less character.

options.label: A new salvaging skill
options.description: Buys: scavenging becomes a named skill on every pawn, the strongest statement of identity. Costs: a new skill touches every pawn, every mod's skill screens and balance; the most expensive and riskiest.

questions.question: Should some salvaged parts come out unidentified until a Jawa appraises them?

options.label: Yes, rare finds only (Recommended)
options.description: Why: keeps the surprise special. Buys: a corroded part that a good appraiser reveals as a prize; an appraiser role. Costs: one extra job per rare find and a new item per size.

options.label: Yes, everything from a wreck
options.description: Buys: every haul is a mystery box. Costs: sorting becomes a chore, and players stop caring about the reveal.

options.label: No, parts arrive known
options.description: Buys: simplest, no extra job. Costs: no treasure-hunt moment; skill only changes how much you get.

questions.question: Besides raw skill, how should the clan get better at scavenging?

options.label: Tools and droid help
options.description: Buys: progress through research: a hydrospanner, a cutting torch, a salvage droid module for lethal maps. Costs: art for each tool and a droid module; a week or so.

options.label: Jawa gene and traits
options.description: Buys: makes the Jawa description's 'instinct for salvage' true, cheap XML, colonists known as the appraiser. Costs: changes every Jawa including traders; no research path.

options.label: Both, on one shared number (Recommended)
options.description: Why: one stat keeps bonuses from stacking into nonsense. Buys: the gene and the first tools both feed one salvage rating. Costs: the most balancing, and the tool art.

options.label: Skill only, nothing more
options.description: Buys: nothing to build or balance. Costs: no progression beyond skill, and the Jawa identity stays words, not numbers.

questions.question: Should a Jawa be able to choose how to cut a wreck apart?

options.label: Yes: quick, careful or gut one part
options.description: Buys: a real decision on every wreck, the closest thing to a scavenging minigame; on a lethal map time on site matters. Costs: two weeks, balance work, and more clicks per wreck.

options.label: Only 'gut one part'
options.description: Buys: aim at the drive or power cell and leave the rest; one clear choice. Costs: still a new button and job; less depth than three modes.

options.label: Not now, after the core ships (Recommended)
options.description: Why: worth it once hauls are worth protecting. Buys: the core ships sooner. Costs: no on-site choice until later.

questions.question: Should surveying a wreck before stripping it reveal its story and hazards?

options.label: Hazards and loot tier only
options.description: Buys: pick which wreck is worth the trip on a lethal map; warns of nests and live charges. Costs: about a week; a short extra job, optional.

options.label: Also lore and leads
options.description: Buys: wrecks with names and manifests that point to cargo still out there, feeding quests and the antiquities tree. Costs: lots of writing, and each lead needs a quest to point at.

options.label: Later, once leads have quests (Recommended)
options.description: Why: a lead with nowhere to go is a tooltip. Buys: no writing debt now. Costs: wrecks stay resource piles for a while.

options.label: No survey step
options.description: Buys: nothing to build, no extra step. Costs: wrecks never carry stories.

questions.question: The clan's crashed-ship landmark sits on every desert map, but the new wreck law calls deserts travelled land; what should happen to it?

options.label: Make it rare (Recommended)
options.description: Why: matches your law without losing the landmark. Buys: finding one becomes an event. Costs: most desert maps lose their one big wreck.

options.label: Keep it on every desert map
options.description: Buys: the clan's home ground keeps its familiar landmark. Costs: breaks the law that travelled land is cleaned within decades.

options.label: Move it to the deep desert only
options.description: Buys: the wreck sits where few go, which the law likes. Costs: the ordinary desert has no big wreck at all.

options.label: Remove it
options.description: Buys: the cleanest reading of the law. Costs: throws away built content and the start area's one landmark.

questions.question: Should a part's revealed grade change what traders pay, and may a Jawa bluff about it?

options.label: Grade sets price, no bluffing
options.description: Buys: good appraisal pays at every trader at once, simple. Costs: a few days; no trickster play.

options.label: Grade sets price, bluff in haggling (Recommended)
options.description: Why: the Jawa trader at full strength. Buys: pass junk off as good during the haggle, with a reputation cost if caught. Costs: waits on the haggle screen, which is planned but not built.

options.label: Grade is flavour only
options.description: Buys: nothing to balance in trade. Costs: appraisal pays only through use, not sale.
